props.note: Bismarck's hull, repositioned 2026-09 to the H.M.S. Hood Association's 2001 expedition fix (48.15N, 16.117W; see sources.md for the position discrepancy this replaced and the residual depth-vs-terrain gap at this point). Length 251 m and beam 36 m are the ship's published overall dimensions (Wikipedia, data/landmarks.json wreck_meta). Height 15 m is an unsourced estimate for a battleship hull of this displacement; no source found publishes a keel-to-deck figure for the wreck. ends [prow, rounded]: surveys (kbismarck.com) describe the hull as largely intact and in surprisingly good condition, so this uses a pointed bow and a rounded stern rather than a torn 'cut' end; note that data/landmarks.json's own wreck_meta separately describes the bow as 'separated from main hull', which conflicts with the intact-hull account -- see sources.md. heading_deg 20 is arbitrary: no source found publishes the ship's actual compass orientation on the seabed. 2026-09 (F1-WRECKS): the hand-built hull ("wreck": "bismarck") follows docs/research/sites.md instead: upright, stern broken away aft of turret Dora (never found), so 'ends' is now [prow, cut]; the four main turrets fell out on capsizing, leaving empty barbettes. Turret, superstructure and barbette stations follow the ship's general arrangement.

Stands in for Bismarck's four detached main-battery (38 cm) gun turrets, which broke free during the sinking and came to rest roughly in a line down the seamount flank (kbismarck.org forum, citing 1989 and later survey accounts; Magellan's 2019 digital-twin survey). The engine's procedural kinds have no turret shape, so a debris cluster marks the general area; it does not depict the turrets' real form. No public coordinates were found for the individual turrets, so this placement, roughly 1.2 km up-slope (north-east, toward the seamount summit) of the hull, is illustrative only -- hence low confidence on the matching POI. Repositioned 2026-09 with the hull; see sources.md.

Hull plating, frames and pipes around the torn aft end, where the stern broke away (kbismarck.com wreck summary; the stern itself has never been found). Centred ~130 m astern of the hull (bearing 200 deg from the hull fix, i.e. off the torn end for heading 20). Position, radius and piece counts are illustrative.

The underwater landslide the hull set off as it hit the seamount flank and slid down it (Ballard 1989 survey; docs/research/sites.md: 'build a scrape, small slide blocks'). Sediment blocks and edge berms in an ellipse 400 m long and 90 m wide (dimensions_m = [half-length, half-width, height] for this kit), laid from the hull up-slope toward the turret area (bearing 82 deg). The coarse terrain does not resolve the real scar; its length, width and course here are a reconstruction.
